newsitem.title: UK: Three-year gilts go through the roof in repo mkt.
newsitem.headline: Three-year gilts go through the roof in repo mkt.

text.p: UK gilts due 1999 traded at unheard of levels of expense in the repo market on Friday, dealers said.
The 6.0 percent, three-year gilts traded at 1.5 percent and even lower overnight, while overnight general collateral rates hovered above 6.0 percent in early trade.
Dealers said the stock was being pushed by large short positions.
"The 6.0 percents of '99 traded as low as 1.5 percent and maybe even as low as one percent," one repo trader said. "There are some genuine shorts on this one rather than a squeeze."
The trader said the Bank of England had not been seen to act. It has committed itself to ironing out anomolies in the gilt repo market if stocks are squeezed by market participants.
One week GC rates were trading at 5.85/5.75 percent in late trade, while one month rates stood at 5.67/5.63 percent.
In the money market, another large shortage saw unsecured cash rates head higher.

The Bank forecast a 1.75 billion stg shortage and only took out 46 million stg in early operations. But it later acted more substantially and by the time it gave 70 million stg in unspecified late assistance, it had managed to wipe out the shortage in full.
Money market traders said cash rates tightened early on but in late trade, overnight cash had subsided to 5-15/16, 13/16 percent, having closed at 5-3/4, 1/2 percent on Thursday.
One week rates stood at 5-13/16, 11/16 percent while one month rates were 5-3/4, 11/16 percent.
Money market traders expect next week to be lively with Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George holding their monthly monetary meeting on Wednesday.
Many analysts say the odds of another interest rate cut are evenly balanced.
